I recommend don’t thin, run for fewer iterations, and use default so that warmup is half the total number of iterations.  I think that setting warmup=1000 and iter=10000 is a mistake.  If you really need 10000 iterations, then you should be spending more than 1000 on warmup.
A

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Warning Messages
parts:
On Sunday, October 25, 2015 at 8:58:08 PM UTC-4, Satwik Acharyya wrote:
How large ??  In my case the count is 8 when i am running 100 simulations.

8% is not great. You may be able to get rid of them with a higher degrees of freedom parameter for the inverse Wishart but we don't recommend using the inverse Wishart distribution in the first place. It is generally much better to parameterize a covariance matrix into the product a diagonal matrix of standard deviations, a correlation matrix,  and the diagonal matrix of standard deviations again. In that case, you can put some reasonable prior on the standard deviations and an lkj_corr(1) prior on the correlation matrix (or even better an lkj_cholesky_corr(1) prior on its Cholesky factor). There are many examples of this reparameterization in the manual and on the Stan-users list.

Ben

If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

This message comes once after every chain. I am running 3 chains then it comes after every chain. Which implies sporadic? I mean how to  
understand it is sporadic or not?
The phrase "this warning" refers to the thing(s) that immediately precede it

Exception thrown at line $93$  normal_log : Location parameter is nan, but must be finite!                  
Exception thrown at line $86$  inv_wishart_log : LDLT Factor of random variable is not positive definit

and those are often numerical problems rather than problems with the Stan code. But I wouldn't consider 8% to be sporadic and it tends to mean that the chain is having difficulty drawing from the tails, which is pretty typical when using an inverse Wishart prior and consequently we do not recommend doing so.

Ben
